question: What is the lower, tapered end of the spinal cord called?
explanation: The conus medullaris marks the normal lower end of the spinal cord in adults. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T24#GNS211_U3_T24_h1)

question: Why do the lower nerve roots form a horse-tail shape known as the cauda equina?

options.A: Nerve roots ascend from the sacrum to the brainstem
options.B: Cerebrospinal fluid pushes the nerves downward over time
options.C: The spinal column grows faster than the spinal cord
options.D: The spinal cord sheds excess nervous tissue daily

explanation: Because the backbone grows faster than the spinal cord, the lower nerve roots have to trail downward inside the canal to reach their exit points. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T24#GNS211_U3_T24_h1)

question: Which membrane lies directly on the surface of the spinal cord?
explanation: The pia mater is the delicate innermost layer that hugs the surface of the spinal cord. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T24#GNS211_U3_T24_h2)

question: Where is the common site for giving an epidural injection to block pain during childbirth?
explanation: The epidural space is located just outside the tough outer membrane (dura mater) and is the target area for regional nerve blocks. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T24#GNS211_U3_T24_h2)

question: What kind of nerve cells are mainly found in the front (anterior) horns of the spinal cord's grey matter?
explanation: The anterior horns contain motor neuron cell bodies that send signals out to skeletal muscles. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T24#GNS211_U3_T24_h3)

question: What is the main function of the side (lateral) horns in the spinal grey matter?
explanation: The lateral horns handle involuntary body functions like heart rate and digestion through the autonomic nervous system. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T24#GNS211_U3_T24_h3)

question: What is the main job of ascending nerve tracts in the spinal cord?

options.A: Producing cerebrospinal fluid within the canal
options.B: Regulating baseline heart rate and breathing
options.C: Delivering motor commands to skeletal muscles
options.D: Carrying sensory information to the brain

explanation: Ascending tracts act like pathways carrying touch, pain, and temperature signals upward from the body to the brain. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T24#GNS211_U3_T24_h4)

question: A patient with damage to their lateral corticospinal tracts will likely have which symptom?

options.A: Inability to regulate resting blood pressure levels
options.B: Complete absence of involuntary spinal reflexes
options.C: Impaired voluntary movement on the affected side
options.D: Total loss of conscious pain and temperature perception

explanation: Corticospinal tracts are the main pathways responsible for controlling conscious, skilled body movements. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T24#GNS211_U3_T24_h4)

question: What structure is found inside the dorsal root of a spinal nerve?
explanation: The dorsal root ganglion contains the cell bodies of sensory neurons bringing incoming signals into the spinal cord. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T24#GNS211_U3_T24_h5)

question: What is a dermatome?

options.A: An area of skin supplied by a single spinal nerve
options.B: The protective outer sheath wrapping a peripheral nerve
options.C: A reflex center located inside the lumbar grey matter
options.D: A surgical instrument used to cut thin skin grafts

explanation: Dermatomes map out which areas of skin send signals to specific spinal nerves, helping nurses assess nerve injuries. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T24#GNS211_U3_T24_h5)

question: What is the final part of a standard reflex arc that carries out the action?
explanation: The effector is the muscle or gland that performs the final action in response to a reflex. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T24#GNS211_U3_T24_h6)

question: Why are spinal reflexes important for the body?

options.A: They replace the need for sensory input from the skin
options.B: They prevent all forms of muscle fatigue during exercise
options.C: They allow the brain to consciously plan complex movements
options.D: They trigger quick protective reactions without waiting for brain processing

explanation: Reflexes bypass the brain to create lightning-fast protective movements, like pulling your hand away from a hot stove. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T24#GNS211_U3_T24_h6)

question: What term describes paralysis of both lower limbs caused by a lower spinal cord injury?
explanation: Paraplegia is the loss of movement and sensation in the lower half of the body. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T24#GNS211_U3_T24_h7)

question: Why is a high neck (cervical) spinal cord injury a medical emergency?

options.A: It destroys the main blood supply to the brainstem
options.B: It causes permanent loss of bowel control without other symptoms
options.C: It immediately stops all thinking in the brain
options.D: It can paralyze the diaphragm and stop breathing

explanation: The nerves controlling the diaphragm (the main breathing muscle) originate in the cervical spine. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T24#GNS211_U3_T24_h7)
